practiceQuestions.q: Which Article of the Indian Constitution explicitly mentions the parliamentary privileges of the Houses of Parliament, their members, and committees?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 105 of the Indian Constitution deals with the powers, privileges, etc., of the Houses of Parliament and of the members and committees thereof. Article 102 is about disqualifications, Article 110 defines Money Bills, and Article 122 bars courts from inquiring into parliamentary proceedings.

practiceQuestions.q: Parliamentary privileges available in India are primarily derived from which country's parliamentary system?
practiceQuestions.sol: Before the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act (1978), Article 105(3) explicitly equated Indian parliamentary privileges to those of the British House of Commons at the time of the commencement of the Constitution. Even after the amendment removed the explicit reference, British precedents heavily influence Indian parliamentary practice regarding privileges.

practiceQuestions.q: Which constitutional amendment act removed the direct reference to the British House of Commons in Article 105(3)?
practiceQuestions.sol: The 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978 amended Article 105(3) to state that the privileges of the members of Parliament shall be those as may from time to time be defined by Parliament, and until so defined, shall be those of the House of Commons as of the date of commencement of the Constitution.

practiceQuestions.q: Which Article of the Constitution extends parliamentary privileges to persons who have the right to speak in and otherwise take part in the proceedings of Parliament, such as the Attorney General of India?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 88 states that every Minister and the Attorney General of India shall have the right to speak in, and otherwise to take part in the proceedings of, either House, any joint sitting of the Houses, and any committee of Parliament of which he may be named a member, but shall not by virtue of this article be entitled to a vote. Consequently, parliamentary privileges apply to them during such proceedings.

practiceQuestions.q: Which Article deals with the parliamentary privileges of State Legislatures in India?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 194 of the Indian Constitution corresponds to Article 105 and deals with the powers, privileges, etc., of the Houses of State Legislatures and of the members and committees thereof.

practiceQuestions.q: How are parliamentary privileges broadly classified into categories in Indian parliamentary practice?
opts: Those enjoyed by each House collectively and those enjoyed by members individually
practiceQuestions.sol: Parliamentary privileges are broadly classified into two categories: (1) those that are enjoyed by each House of Parliament collectively, and (2) those that are enjoyed by the members individually.

practiceQuestions.q: During sessions of Parliament and for how many days before and after sessions are members immune from arrest in civil cases?
opts: No immunity in civil cases exists
practiceQuestions.sol: Under the Code of Civil Procedure, members of Parliament are exempt from arrest in civil cases during the continuance of the session of the House and for 40 days before its commencement and 40 days after its conclusion. This immunity does not apply to criminal cases or preventive detention.

practiceQuestions.q: Can a member of Parliament be arrested for a criminal offence (such as a criminal charge or under preventive detention) while the House is in session?
opts: Yes, criminal immunity does not exist; members can be arrested anytime for criminal offenses.
No, prior permission of the Speaker/Chairman is mandatory for any arrest inside Parliament House only.
Yes, but only after a two-thirds majority resolution passed by the House.
No, MPs have absolute immunity from arrest for any offense during their entire tenure.
practiceQuestions.sol: Privilege of freedom from arrest is limited only to civil cases. Members can be arrested in criminal cases, under preventive detention, or for contempt of court just like any ordinary citizen, though the arresting authorities must inform the Speaker/Chairman immediately.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following is NOT a collective privilege of Parliament?
opts: Right to publish debates, proceedings, and reports
Freedom of speech in Parliament for members
Right to exclude strangers (non-members) from proceedings
Right to punish members and outsiders for breach of privilege or contempt
practiceQuestions.sol: Freedom of speech in Parliament is an individual privilege enjoyed by the members (under Article 105(1)). The other three options are collective privileges enjoyed by each House of Parliament as a body.

practiceQuestions.q: Who holds the final authority to decide whether a breach of parliamentary privilege or contempt of the House has occurred?
opts: The Privileges Committee of the respective House
The House itself (Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha)
practiceQuestions.sol: Each House of Parliament is the absolute judge of its own privileges. It has the sole authority to decide whether a breach of privilege or contempt has occurred and what punishment should be meted out.

practiceQuestions.q: Why are parliamentary privileges considered essential for the functioning of a democratic legislature?
opts: To grant MPs legal immunity from paying corporate taxes on their assets.
To safeguard the independence, authority, and dignity of Parliament against external interference or executive overreach.
To elevate parliamentarians to a superior legal status above the ordinary judiciary permanently.
To prevent citizens from filing RTI applications regarding parliamentary expenses.
practiceQuestions.sol: Parliamentary privileges are not designed to create a privileged class of citizens, but to protect lawmakers from obstruction, intimidation, or executive pressure, ensuring they can debate, question, and legislate without fear or favor.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the principle of judicial review interact with the exercise of parliamentary privileges in India?
opts: Courts have absolute jurisdiction to review and overturn any decision made by Parliament regarding its privileges.
Courts cannot interfere under any circumstances with internal proceedings or privilege rulings of Parliament.
While internal proceedings are protected, if a privilege ruling violates fundamental rights (like Article 21) or constitutional provisions, courts can examine it.
Judicial review applies only to State Legislatures, not to the Parliament of India.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Supreme Court has held that although Parliament is the sole judge of its privileges, if a privilege decision or punishment violates fundamental rights (e.g., right to life and personal liberty under Article 21) or basic constitutional provisions, it is subject to judicial review (e.g., Keshav Singh Case, 1965).

practiceQuestions.q: What is the constitutional status regarding the codification of parliamentary privileges in India?
opts: Parliament has comprehensively codified all privileges into a single statute.
Codification is constitutionally prohibited by Article 105.
Parliament has not codified privileges into a single law; instead, they rely on constitutional provisions, parliamentary laws, rules of procedure, and British precedents.
Privileges are codified only for Rajya Sabha, but not for Lok Sabha.
practiceQuestions.sol: Parliament has consciously avoided codifying privileges because codification would make them subject to judicial review in every single instance, whereas leaving them uncodified gives the Houses flexibility to deal with unforeseen breaches. Article 105(3) empowers Parliament to define them by law, but it has chosen not to enact a comprehensive code.

practiceQuestions.q: How does freedom of speech inside Parliament under Article 105(1) interact with other constitutional limitations, such as the conduct of Supreme Court and High Court judges?
opts: MPs can discuss the personal conduct of judges without any restriction during parliamentary debates.
Article 121 explicitly prohibits discussion in Parliament with respect to the conduct of any judge of the Supreme Court or High Court in the discharge of duties, except upon a motion for impeachment.
Judges' conduct can be freely discussed if approved by a majority vote of the Privileges Committee.
Freedom of speech overrides all other articles, permitting unrestricted criticism of the judiciary.
practiceQuestions.sol: While Article 105(2) provides immunity for anything said in Parliament, Article 121 places a vital constitutional restriction: no discussion shall take place in Parliament regarding the conduct of any judge of the Supreme Court or High Court in the discharge of their duties, except when considering an impeachment motion.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the scope of protection provided to publication of parliamentary proceedings under Article 105(2)?
opts: Absolute protection for any publication made by anyone, anywhere, under any circumstances.
No protection exists for publication; newspapers can be sued for defamation for reporting parliamentary debates.

Protection applies to true reports of parliamentary proceedings published under the authority of the House (Parliamentary Proceedings (Protection of Publication) Act, 1956 extends this to substantially true media reports without malice).
Only official government gazettes are protected; private newspapers are excluded entirely.
practiceQuestions.sol: While Article 105(2) protects official publication under the authority of the House, the Parliamentary Proceedings (Protection of Publication) Act, 1956 (also known as Feroze Gandhi Act) provides that no person shall be civilly or criminally liable for publishing a substantially true report of parliamentary proceedings, provided it is not published with malice.

practiceQuestions.q: If a member of Parliament is prosecuted for accepting a bribe to vote or speak in a particular manner in Parliament, does the privilege of freedom of speech under Article 105(2) shield them from criminal prosecution?
opts: Yes, because voting and speaking are core parliamentary proceedings protected by immunity.
No, the Supreme Court (in Sita Soren case, 2024) ruled that bribery is not protected by parliamentary privilege and MPs can be prosecuted under anti-corruption laws.
Yes, unless the Privileges Committee explicitly waives immunity.
Only the Speaker can decide whether bribery charges can be investigated by police.
practiceQuestions.sol: In the landmark 2024 Supreme Court ruling in the Sita Soren v. Union of India case (overruling the 1998 PV Narasimha Rao judgment), a 7-judge Constitution bench held that parliamentary privileges do not extend to corruption or bribery. Taking a bribe to speak or vote in Parliament is a criminal act and is not immune from prosecution.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the procedure followed by the House when a question of breach of privilege is raised?
opts: The matter is automatically referred to the Supreme Court for adjudication.
First, consent of the Presiding Officer (Speaker/Chairman) is required; if given, the House may discuss it or refer it to the Privileges Committee.
Any member can directly arrest the alleged violator and bring them to the well of the House.
The Prime Minister decides whether a privilege motion is admissible.
practiceQuestions.sol: To raise a question of breach of privilege, a member must give notice and obtain the consent of the Speaker or Chairman. If the Presiding Officer gives consent, the member can seek leave of the House to move a motion, which may then be discussed by the House or referred to the Committee of Privileges for detailed examination and report.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the power to regulate internal proceedings (Article 122) relate to parliamentary privileges?
opts: It allows courts to examine procedural irregularities in passing any bill.
It bars courts from inquiring into proceedings of Parliament on the ground of any alleged irregularity of procedure, ensuring legislative autonomy.
It mandates that all parliamentary rules must be approved by the Supreme Court before implementation.
It gives executive ministers power to suspend parliamentary rules during emergencies.

practiceQuestions.q: What remedies or punishments can the Parliament impose for breach of privilege or contempt of the House?
opts: Capital punishment and life imprisonment only.
Admonition, reprimand, suspension from the House for a period, or imprisonment (for outsiders/members during the session).
Financial fines up to 10 crore rupees for breaching privilege.
Permanent disqualification from contesting future elections determined by the Speaker alone.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Houses of Parliament possess punitive powers to punish those found guilty of breach of privilege or contempt. Punishments include admonition, reprimand, suspension from service of the House (for members), and imprisonment or commitment to custody (applicable to both members and outsiders, but imprisonment of members lasts only during the session).

practiceQuestions.q: Can a witness summoned before a parliamentary committee claim privilege against self-incrimination?
opts: No witness can refuse to answer questions before a parliamentary committee on any grounds.
Yes, parliamentary committees have no power to compel testimony.

While parliamentary committees possess wide powers to summon witnesses and examine them on oath, constitutional protections like Article 20(3) (self-incrimination) and laws of evidence generally apply, though parliamentary privilege gives committees strong coercive powers.
Witnesses are strictly prohibited from speaking truth if it harms the government.
practiceQuestions.sol: Parliamentary committees have extensive powers to summon witnesses, inspect documents, and take evidence. However, constitutional guarantees such as the right against self-incrimination (Article 20(3)) and legal norms protect individuals, though refusal to answer legitimate parliamentary committee questions without lawful excuse can constitute contempt of the House.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Parliamentary Privileges in India:
1. They are available to both the Houses of Parliament and their committees only, excluding individual members.
2. They are incorporated under Article 105 of the Constitution of India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because parliamentary privileges are available to individual members of Parliament as well (e.g., freedom of speech, freedom from civil arrest). Statement 2 is correct because Article 105 explicitly deals with the powers, privileges, etc., of Parliament, its members, and committees.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about individual parliamentary privileges:
1. Members enjoy freedom of speech and expression in Parliament, subject to the provisions of the Constitution and the rules/standing orders of the House.
2. Members are completely immune from arrest in all criminal and civil cases during their entire tenure including non-session periods.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct; freedom of speech in Parliament is subject to constitutional provisions (like Article 121) and the rules of procedure. Statement 2 is incorrect because immunity from arrest applies ONLY to civil cases, and that too during sessions and 40 days before/after; members have no immunity from criminal arrest or preventive detention.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding collective privileges of Parliament:
1. The right to exclude strangers (non-members) from the proceedings of the House is a collective privilege.
2. The Parliament has the power to prohibit the publication of its debates and proceedings by external media outlets.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Each House possesses the collective right to exclude strangers from its chamber at any time to hold secret sittings. It also holds the right to prohibit the publication of its proceedings, though under the Feroze Gandhi Act, substantially true reports published without malice are protected.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the codification of parliamentary privileges:
1. The Constitution of India explicitly mandates that Parliament must enact a comprehensive law to codify all privileges within 10 years of commencement.
2. Indian Parliament has deliberately chosen not to codify its privileges into a single statute to retain flexibility.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because the Constitution does not mandate codification within any timeframe; it only enables Parliament to define them by law if it so wishes. Statement 2 is correct; Parliament has not enacted a comprehensive code because codification would make all privileges subject to strict judicial review and limit the House's disciplinary flexibility.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the relationship between Fundamental Rights and Parliamentary Privileges:
1. Parliamentary privileges enshrined in Article 105 override Part III (Fundamental Rights) of the Constitution entirely.
2. The Supreme Court has ruled that a parliamentary privilege exercise must harmonize with Fundamental Rights, particularly Article 21.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect; Article 105 is subject to the provisions of the Constitution, including Fundamental Rights. Statement 2 is correct because the Supreme Court has clarified that exercise of parliamentary privileges is subject to fundamental rights, and courts can review privilege decisions if they violate personal liberty or fundamental guarantees.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Committee of Privileges in Parliament:
1. It is a standing committee consisting of nominated members in both Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha.
2. Its function is to investigate cases of breach of privilege referred to it and recommend appropriate action to the House.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The Committee of Privileges is a standing parliamentary committee (Lok Sabha committee has 15 members; Rajya Sabha committee has 10 members) nominated by the Speaker/Chairman. It examines cases of breach of privilege referred by the Presiding Officer and submits a report with recommendations.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding judicial immunity and parliamentary proceedings:
1. Courts are prohibited from inquiring into the internal proceedings of Parliament under Article 122.
2. If a member commits a criminal offence inside the House during a sitting, police can enter the chamber and arrest them without the Speaker's permission.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct; Article 122 bars courts from questioning parliamentary proceedings on procedural irregularity grounds. Statement 2 is incorrect because no arrest (criminal or civil) can be made within the precincts of the House (chamber or lobby) without obtaining the prior permission of the Speaker/Chairman, regardless of where the crime occurred.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the application of parliamentary privileges to non-members:
1. Ministers who are not members of either House of Parliament enjoy the same parliamentary privileges as elected MPs when participating in parliamentary proceedings.
2. Private citizens or media houses can be held liable for contempt of the House if they publish malicious or distorted reports of parliamentary debates.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Under Article 88, ministers and the Attorney General have the right to speak and participate in proceedings, thereby enjoying relevant privileges during such participation. Furthermore, outsiders, including media houses and private citizens, are subject to parliamentary jurisdiction for breach of privilege or contempt (such as publishing malicious reports or defaming the House).

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the historical evolution of parliamentary privileges in India:
1. The 44th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1978 removed the specific reference to the British House of Commons in Article 105(3).
2. Prior to 1978, Indian parliamentary privileges were legally identical to those of the British House of Commons at the commencement of the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Original Article 105(3) stated that privileges would be those of the British House of Commons until defined by Parliament. The 44th Amendment Act 1978 substituted this reference, stating privileges would be those defined by Parliament or as existing immediately before the amendment.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the scope of freedom of speech under Article 105:
1. An MP cannot be prosecuted in any court of law for anything said or any vote given by them in Parliament or any committee thereof.
2. This immunity extends to statements made by MPs outside the Parliament house or in press conferences during the inter-session period.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct and directly reflects Article 105(2). Statement 2 is incorrect because freedom of speech and immunity under Article 105 applies strictly to statements made *inside* Parliament or its committees during parliamentary proceedings; statements made outside, in press conferences, or public rallies do not enjoy parliamentary immunity and are subject to normal civil/criminal laws (e.g., defamation).
